text:
The court should apply Washington law and deny the punitive damages claim, because Washington's strong public policy against punitive damages, applied through its most-significant-relationship analysis, lets the forum refuse California's rule (I recall *Dailey v. North Coast Life Ins. Co.* (Wash. 1996) from memory and have not re-checked it). The shared note is wrong: state punitive damages law is not uniform, and California allows punitive damages only on clear and convincing proof of malice, oppression, or fraud (Cal. Civ. Code § 3294), not to prevailing parties generally.

CONFIDENCE: 60
